title: QaWaiver
description: A named human's immutable decision to accept specific WARNING-severity QA findings (decisions.md D-35). Three properties make this a control rather than a formality: (1) it names the findings it covers by id, so it cannot be a blanket 'proceed'; (2) it names a human approver, so a waiver is always attributable; (3) it can never cover a blocker — source/timebase faults, corrupt or missing media, rights failures, missing required captions or disclosures, and invalid output are non-waivable, and the gate REJECTS a waiver that names one rather than ignoring it. Rejecting rather than ignoring is deliberate: an ignored waiver leaves the operator believing the finding was accepted.

changelog.reason: Initial v1 (Phase 4, task 9; D-35). `findingIds` is `minItems: 1` because an empty waiver is either a mistake or an attempt to pre-authorise whatever a later run finds — neither should validate.

Added required `planHash`, and moved the gate scope onto it. Scoping on `renderId` alone was unusable: a waiver is written against a failing render and applied by RE-rendering, which mints a new renderId, so every waiver was rejected as out of scope. Scoping on nothing was worse — most warning findings carry no time range, so ids like `true_peak:audio` are identical across every render of every job and one waiver file would have waived that warning permanently. The plan hash is the identity a human acceptance actually has.

renderId.description: The render whose findings were reviewed. Recorded for provenance — WHICH execution the human actually looked at — but not what the gate scopes on; see `planHash`.

findingIds.description: The specific `TechnicalQaFinding.findingId` values accepted. Finding ids are derived from (checkId, object, time range), so they are stable across a re-run of QA over the SAME render and unstable across a different render — which is exactly the scope a waiver should have.

approvedBy.description: The named human accepting the findings (decisions.md D-9: acceptance is a human act recorded with a name). Not a role, not a system identity.

reason.description: Why the warnings are acceptable for this render. Required — an unexplained waiver is indistinguishable from a rubber stamp six months later.

planHash.description: The render PLAN this waiver accepts — sha256 over the resolved manifest, clip ranges and caption files, excluding absolute paths. This, not `renderId`, is what the gate scopes on: `renderId` is minted fresh by every execution, so scoping on it made a waiver unusable (write a waiver naming the failing render, re-render to apply it, and the new render has a new id). `planHash` is stable across re-renders of the SAME plan and changes the moment any editorial or encode input changes — which is exactly the scope a human acceptance has.
